tone_statements.citation: Viljoen, Melanie. 2017. The Gavar Verb Phrase. Yaounde: SIL / Ministry of Scientific Research and Innovation. 108 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Gavar verb roots are underlying toneless. Their surface tone is influenced by the types of consonants and vowels they contain. Tone spreading also occurs from verb prefixes. [...] [footnote 4:] Gavar appears to have two underlying level tones, low and high. However the influence of depressor and raisor consonants may result in a surface mid tone. More research needs to be done into the tonal system of other grammatical categories to confirm this hypothesis.
tone_statements.locator: p.13, sec. 2.3 'Tone on verb roots', opening paragraph; footnote 4 printed at the foot of p.15, anchored to point 1 'The default surface tone on verbs is mid.' in the six-point summary on p.15
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 underlying level (L, H); 3 surface (H, M, L)

tone_statements.citation: Viljoen, Melanie H. 2009. Precis d'orthographe pour la langue gavar. Edition preliminaire. Yaounde: SIL Cameroun. 37 pp.
tone_statements.quote: 3 Les tons. On a identifié trois tons de surface en gavar : haut, moyen et bas. 3.1 Les oppositions de tons lexicaux marqués par des signes diacritiques. Au niveau où on est parvenu, on a découvert plusieurs paires minimales de tons pour des mots qui opposent les tons moyen et bas, les tons haut et moyen et les tons haut et bas. Cependant, les paires minimales sont rares. En plus il s'agit souvent des mots qui appartiennent aux classes grammaticales différentes. Autrement la signification pourrait être déterminée pas le contexte. On propose alors une orthographe dans laquelle le ton lexical n'est pas indiqué.
tone_statements.translation: 3 Tones. Three surface tones have been identified in Gavar: high, mid and low. 3.1 Lexical tone oppositions marked by diacritics. At the stage reached so far, several tonal minimal pairs have been found for words opposing mid and low, high and mid, and high and low tones. However, minimal pairs are rare. Moreover they are often words belonging to different grammatical classes. Otherwise the meaning could be determined by context. We therefore propose an orthography in which lexical tone is not indicated.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 3 'Les tons' and 3.1: (footer-p.12; the document's own TOC lists 3.1/3.2 at p.13)

tone.says: Held full text read (sec. 2.3 'Tone on verb roots' pp.13-15 and Appendix A): 120 verbs recorded in four tonal frames; verb roots underlyingly toneless; consonants split into depressor (voiced obstruents), raiser (voiceless obstruents and implosives) and neutral (sonorants); default surface tone on verbs is mid; depressors lower tone; raisers permit H spreading from a prefix; L spreading from a prefix frequent but may be blocked by raisers; closed vowels more susceptible to spreading; footnote 4…

sources.note: Sec. 5.3.2 Daba group: Gavar (data from Noukeu 2004) has lost vowel prosodies, four vowels /a ə i e/, /s/ vs /ʃ/ contrast; the reconstruction explicitly excludes tone and stress; nothing on Gavar stress.

sources.citation: Viljoen, Melanie Helen. 2013. A Grammatical Description of the Buwal Language. PhD thesis, La Trobe University. doi:10.26181/21845661.v1 (Buwal, buwa1243, Gavar's closest relative)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Describes Buwal, not Gavar. Sec. 1.1.4 'Linguistic relationship with Gavar' and scattered comparative notes (author's Gavar fieldnotes) contain nothing on Gavar prosody; for Buwal itself ch. 2 treats tone only and p.87 remarks that Chadic metrical structure 'is not stress (as normally understood in terms of higher pitch or intensity) but has to do with syllable weight', with no such interaction found in Buwal. No Gavar stress statement.

sources.citation: Viljoen, Melanie H. 2009. Precis d'orthographe pour la langue gavar. Edition preliminaire. Yaounde: SIL Cameroun. 37 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 gives consonant/vowel inventories and syllable rules; sec. 3 'Les tons' (p.13) states three surface tones (haut, moyen, bas), lexical tone not. the only 'accent' in the document is 'accent aigu' (the diacritic chosen for the 3PL subject pronoun). No word on stress/accent as prominence.
